title: Poker glossary
lead: Find the terms you hear at the table, explore by category, and learn the language of the game.

terms.definition: A small required amount each player contributes before a hand begins.
terms.example: With a 1-chip ante, everyone puts in 1 chip before cards are dealt.

terms.definition: A required bet made before cards are dealt, usually as a small blind and big blind.
The smaller forced bet posted before the hand by the player left of the button.
The forced bet posted by the player left of the small blind; it sets the table's minimum bet.
The marker for the dealer position. It moves clockwise each hand and determines positions.
Where a player sits relative to the dealer, which determines when they act in a hand.
Under the gun: the first position to act after the big blind preflop.
The seat immediately right of the button, with a late-action advantage in most hands.
To pass your turn without putting in chips when no bet is facing you.
To put the first chips into the pot during a betting round.
To match the current bet to continue in the hand.
To increase the current bet, requiring later players to put in more chips.
To raise again after another player has raised.
To give up your hand and stop competing for the pot.
To bet all the chips you have in front of you.
The total chips players have bet, awarded to the winner of the hand.
A separate pot created from bets an all-in player cannot match, contested by the other players.
The pot size compared with the amount you must pay to continue; it helps judge whether a call is worthwhile.
Unseen cards that could likely turn your hand into a winner.
Your estimated share of the pot over time based on the cards currently known.
The betting round before any community cards are revealed.
The first three community cards dealt face up after the opening betting round.
The fourth community card, revealed after the flop.
The fifth and final community card dealt to the board.
The stage after the final betting round when remaining players reveal cards to determine the winner.
All the face-up community cards available for every player to use.
The shared face-up cards dealt to the table in Hold'em and Omaha.
The face-down cards dealt to each player, visible only to that player.
A side card that helps decide the winner when the main hand is tied.
The best hand currently possible given the board and cards in play.
An incomplete hand that can improve if a suitable card arrives.
Four cards of the same suit that can make a flush with one more card.
A hand that needs a suitable card to complete a five-card straight.
A straight draw missing one rank in the middle, with only four rank cards that complete it.
A straight draw that can complete on either end, with eight possible rank cards.
Betting a weak hand to try to make stronger hands fold.
Betting a draw that may be behind now but can improve into a strong hand.
A bet with a strong hand, hoping weaker hands will call.
A bet on a later round by the player who made the last raise preflop.
Entering preflop by calling the big blind instead of raising.
Playing a very strong hand passively to keep opponents in the hand.
To check first, then raise after an opponent bets.
To discard cards face down without showing them, usually a losing hand.
A card set aside face down before the next face-up card to make deck order harder to predict.
A fee taken by a poker room from pots or tournaments for hosting the game.
The amount required to enter a game or tournament.
The total chips a player has in front of them at the table.
A player or chip stack with relatively few chips compared with others at the table.
Making careless decisions after emotions pull you away from your plan.
A forced opening bet in stud games, made by the player with a specified exposed card.
A stage of dealing and betting, such as the flop or river.
The first exposed card dealt to a player in a stud game.
A game format where one part of the pot goes to the highest hand and another to a qualifying lowest hand.
A rule requiring a low hand's highest card to be an 8 or lower to qualify for the low pot.
A-2-3-4-5, the lowest possible straight; it also counts as a straight.
Winning both the high and low portions of a split pot game.
A draw poker variant where four cards of different ranks and suits are important.
A poker variant won by the lowest hand; aces are high, and straights and flushes count against you.
A Hold'em variant played with a 36-card deck, usually with the 2–5 cards removed.
A mixed game rotating through Hold'em, Omaha Hi-Lo, Razz, Seven Card Stud, and Eight-or-Better.
A structure where you can bet any amount above the legal minimum, up to your stack.
A structure where the largest bet or raise is limited by the current pot.
A structure where bet and raise sizes are set in advance.
A maximum limit on the number or size of raises in a betting round.
A hand or table where only two players compete against each other.
A playing style that selects and plays relatively few hands.
A playing style that enters the pot with many starting hands.
A playing style that takes initiative with frequent bets and raises.
A playing style that tends to check and call instead of betting or raising.
Slang for a player who is often inexperienced or makes weak decisions.
Slang for an experienced player who regularly takes advantage of opponents' mistakes.
A tournament with no entry fee; also, in split-pot play, a chance to win one half without risking the other.
When a hand that appears far ahead loses to an opponent's lucky later cards.
A situation where two players both have very strong hands and the loss often seems unavoidable.
The set of possible hands a player could hold in a given situation.
A bet using a late-position advantage to win or control the pot.
A pocket pair higher than the highest rank on the board.
A pair made by matching one of your hole cards with the highest card on the board.
A pocket pair matched by one card of the same rank on the board to make three of a kind.
Three cards of the same rank, often made when a paired board matches one of your cards.
A five-card hand combining three of a kind and a pair.
To check in position after the previous player checks, closing the action for the round.
To call a bet and a raise without having put chips in during that round yet.
The smaller of two players' stacks, which sets how many chips they can win from each other.
The tournament stage just before players reach the paid places.
